title: PCASim: Promptable Closed-loop Adversarial Simulation for Urban Traffic Environment

control_signal.value: Natural-language description of the desired adversarial scenario (for example an opposing vehicle cutting into the ego lane at an intersection) supplied by the user.

control_mechanism.value: RAG over an adversarial scenario corpus (Sentence-BERT, FAISS) with few-shot, chain-of-thought prompting makes an LLM write a DSL; a middleware converts it to Python for highway-env; PPO agents then train ego and adversary behaviour.

base_model.value: LLM (DeepSeek-V3 best of those compared) with RAG, DSL-to-Python generation, PPO reinforcement learning agents in highway-env, and Bezier-curve trajectory smoothing.

datasets.value: INTERACTION dataset, rule-filtered into a scenario corpus; simulation in a customized highway-env.

metrics.value: DSL generation score (semantic fidelity, executable validity, structure, etc.); TTC and PET distributions, collision rate versus a baseline; collision and timeout rates for braking, straight, turn, lane-change scenarios; maximum heading angle.

controllability_evidence.value: DeepSeek-V3 DSL score 80.17 on 6 held-out scenes (R1 73.83, Qwen2.5-Plus 63.33); collision rate about 8% above baseline; trained ego avoidance lowers collision rate by roughly 30% on average.

stated_limitations.value: Corpus from one dataset with limited diversity; simplified highway-env dynamics; reliance on external LLM APIs; DSL conversion errors; weak traffic-rule reasoning; RL covers only basic maneuvers.

notes: Packet is a short ICRA version. The abstract says 30% obstacle-avoidance gain while Sec. IV-B.5 text says 30% boost in executable scene yield; the controllability claim is mostly qualitative with a held-out set of only 6 scenes.
